advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Harden output-retry exhaustion detection so it does not depend on pydantic-ai's exact 'Exceeded maximum output retries' message string (e.g. pin it with a test or match on the exception subtype/structured field).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:250: `if "Exceeded maximum output retries" not in str(exc):`

`raise _exhausted_output_retries(...)` only fires on the string match; any other UnexpectedModelBehavior text re-raises and falls through interpret_failure's generic LLMUnavailableError arm (run_failure.py:152)
ABSENCE: no test pins the exact pydantic-ai exhaustion message, so a library wording drift would pass CI while breaking the translation
advisory.finding: Output-retry exhaustion is detected by substring-matching pydantic-ai's internal error text: `if "Exceeded maximum output retries" not in str(exc): raise`. This couples rebar's terminal-vs-propagate decision to an undocumented library message string; a wording change or localization in a pydantic-ai upgrade would silently reclassify an exhaustion as an un-translated UnexpectedModelBehavior (swept into the generic LLMUnavailableError provider-outage bucket instead of UnretryableOutputError), changing gate behavior.
scenarios: pydantic-ai upgrade rewords the 'Exceeded maximum output retries' UnexpectedModelBehavior message
exhaustion then misclassified as a provider outage rather than an unretryable output failure

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the _pai_structured docstring to attribute the retries/capabilities wiring to apply_structured_seams rather than build_agent_kwargs.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:110: `run (already wired into` ... `by ``build_agent_kwargs``); this function only`
agent_call.py:356-357: build_agent_kwargs sets `kwargs["capabilities"] = web_caps` only when web_caps is not None and never sets `retries`
runner.py:499: `apply_structured_seams(kwargs, req, candidates, model_settings)` is the actual seam
dropped.finding: The _pai_structured docstring states the wire projection and output-retry counter are 'already wired into kwargs as capabilities / retries by build_agent_kwargs', but build_agent_kwargs only sets `capabilities` for web_caps and never sets `retries`; the actual wiring is done by apply_structured_seams (invoked separately in runner.run). The misattribution will mislead a maintainer tracing where retries/capabilities are seeded.
scenarios: maintainer greps build_agent_kwargs for retries seeding and finds nothing
dropped.suggested_fix: Change 'already wired into kwargs as capabilities / retries by build_agent_kwargs' to '... by apply_structured_seams'.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives a ModelResponse carrying a ToolCallPart through the wire projection and asserts it is always kept (never omitted), regardless of usage/window.
evidence: docstring: "dropping it would orphan the paired tool return on the next request — so it is never a projection candidate"

The oracle (`test_rp01_s2_bounded_op_oracle.py`) scripts only text-only responses; ABSENCE: no test constructs a response with a ToolCallPart and asserts it survives the wire projection. A regression that dropped tool-call turns (e.g. flipping the has_text/tool-call logic) would not be caught.
dropped.finding: The tool-call exclusion contract in `_is_failed_output_response` (a response carrying ANY ToolCallPart is never a projection candidate, so it is never dropped from the retry wire, or the paired tool return would be orphaned) has no test. This is a distinct `return False` branch with a documented safety rationale, but no test in the diff drives a tool-call-bearing ModelResponse through the wire projection to prove it is kept.
scenarios: An agentic tool-calling turn followed by a retry: a bug in the tool-call guard silently omits the tool-call response, orphaning the paired tool return and corrupting the wire.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a runner-level NativeOutput test that a length/max_tokens truncation stays terminal (one call, UnretryableOutputError) and does NOT get concision-reclassified.
evidence: structured_run.py `_run_native_output`: "a truncated native turn stays TERMINAL, no concision retry"
test_silent_success.py:24-29 `test_native_output_path_checks_stop_reason` asserts on `structured.check_stop_reason(reason)` directly, not through the runner's native branch

ABSENCE: no test in the diff drives PydanticAIRunner over a native-routed FunctionModel emitting finish_reason=length and asserts it aborts after ONE call (terminal) rather than recovering via concision retry.
dropped.finding: The rewritten NativeOutput branch (`_run_native_output`) is untested end-to-end. It now attaches `guard_capability()` (terminal, NOT concision-aware) alongside the shared wire projection and `retries={'output': N}`. The design explicitly states a truncated NATIVE turn must stay TERMINAL (no concision retry), unlike the prompted branch — but the only NativeOutput test calls `structured.check_stop_reason(reason)` in isolation and never exercises `_run_native_output`, so nothing proves the native branch does NOT reclassify a length/max_tokens truncation into a recoverable concision retry.
scenarios: A native-output model truncates a turn; a regression that attached the concision_guard (or wired concision reclassification) to the native branch would let a truncated native turn spuriously recover instead of degrading to INDETERMINATE.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a truncation test whose signal is only in provider_details['finish_reason'] (finish_reason=None) and assert it is reclassified into a concision retry.
evidence: pai_retry.py:104-107 second-layer read: `if isinstance(details, dict) and details.get('finish_reason') in _TRUNCATION_REASONS: return True`
docstring: "mirroring ``check_response``'s two layers so a provider_details-only truncation, pydantic-ai #5221, is caught"
ABSENCE: no test emits a response with `finish_reason=None` and `provider_details={'finish_reason': 'length'}` and asserts concision reclassification.
dropped.finding: The provider_details-only TRUNCATION layer of `_response_is_truncated` (the documented pydantic-ai #5221 mirror for the truncation subset) is untested. The oracle asserts the #5221 provider_details-only shape only for REFUSAL (`test_provider_details_only_refusal_stays_terminal`); the truncation test (`test_truncation_is_reclassified_into_a_bounded_concision_retry`) uses only the normalized `finish_reason: 'length'` layer, so the second read `details.get('finish_reason') in _TRUNCATION_REASONS` is never exercised.
scenarios: A provider that reports truncation only under provider_details (the #5221 shape) — a regression removing the second-layer read would silently drop the truncation-to-concision reclassification and the merely-verbose turn would fail terminally.
